title: Truth and Reconciliation Commission (establishment and hearings)
summary: South Africa's Truth and Reconciliation Commission, created under the Promotion of National Unity and Reconciliation Act of 1995, held its first meeting on 16 December 1995 at Archbishop Desmond Tutu's home in Cape Town. It investigated gross human rights violations from March 1960 to May 1994 through three committees and held more than 2,500 hearings, hearing from roughly 21,000 victims.

uncertainty.note: First meeting 16 December 1995; hearings followed over the next years.

as_recorded.value: Promotion of National Unity and Reconciliation Act, No 34 of 1995; mandate March 1960 to May 1994

importance.justification: Landmark truth commission after apartheid; amnesty and victim hearings.

audience_note: Concerns gross human rights violations and victims' testimony under apartheid.

related.because: The post-apartheid government set the commission up under the 1995 Act to deal with abuses from the apartheid period.
